items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: Monk played with my brother Jules's band.

ctx.x: How did Monk Hazel rate in those days? He played good drums.

Monk was a good drum. I don't know whether he was a great reader or not, but like I say... No. I mean... He played with my brother Jules for quite a while. Yeah. In different bands around the world. He played... Then later on he went with... He went with Sharky, see. And when I left Jimmy Darcy in 51, I came down there. Sharky said, man... He said, the guy driving in... He gets knocked out of his skull and he can't play. Yeah. I said, well... Well, Sharky, I don't wanna mess you up. But... You better keep him…
Yeah, well... It'll turn up. I can come back tomorrow... And look at him some more. You have time tomorrow? I... It's alright with me, but I'm saying...

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: And Ray Badu, Leo Addy and myself, the three of us, we used to all go in there, we'd copy all the Baby's licks.

ctx.x: Well, we might ask about drum solos and style of playing drums, the way it used to be and the way it is now. We only have another minute, unless you have something dictated. No, that's not.

Well, we, we, uh, uh, Baby Dodge was the drummer on the boat, you see. And Ray Badu, Leo Addy and myself, the three of us, we used to all go in there, we'd copy all the Baby's licks. So at that time, if you hear, if you heard any one of the three of us, you heard the same thing, because we all played the same, the same licks. But there was never any drum solos, Bill. You got two bars, you got four bars at the most. There was never anything more than, more than four bars. And that's, that's why I can't stand drum…

items.title: Ray Bauduc and Nappy Lamare Interview, 1959-09-09
items.q: I think Monk Hazel made those.

ctx.x: Well, I made some of those. I don't know which one I made on that. Who was it? I think Monk Hazel made those.
Who were your favorite drummers when you were a kid that you listened to?
